recentItems.title: Heritage Day Celebrations 2026
recentItems.description:
#HeritageDay2026  | President Cyril Ramaphosa leads the 2026 National Heritage Day celebrations as South Africans come together to celebrate the cultures, traditions and shared values that connect us. 

This year's celebrations are held under the theme: “Celebrating Our Living Heritage: Strengthening the Ties That Bind Us” 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: A Khoi ceremony is taking place at Castle of Good Hope  ahead of unveiling of a painting of Krotoa.
recentItems.description:
A Khoi ceremony is taking place at the Castle of Good Hope in Cape Town ahead of the unveiling of a painting of Krotoa.  The event marks Heritage Day and pays tribute to a young Khoi girl, who acted as an interpreter for the Dutch, in the 1700’s and who would after the death of her European husband, be banished and treated as an outcast. The CEO of the Castle control board says what happened to young Krotoa continues in the scourge of gender- based violence which is rife in modern day South Africa. 

Credit: Vanessa Poonah

recentItems.title: Heritage Day | Looking beyond food, music and clothing: Xolelwa Kashe-Katiya
recentItems.description:
Heritage Day is more than a celebration of traditions, food, music and clothing. It is an opportunity to explore the stories, values and experiences that shape who we are. 

This Heritage Day, let's look beyond the usual celebrations and ask what our heritage means in our everyday lives and how we can carry it into the future. 

Xolelwa Kashe-Katiya is Project Leader at Indlulamithi SA Scenarios.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Heritage Day | Celebrating King Shaka
recentItems.description:
AmaZulu King MisuZulu kaZwelithini and provincial government will begin Heritage Day by paying their respects and laying a wreath at the grave of King Shaka.

The main commemoration will take place at the King Zwelithini Stadium in Umlazi.

King Shaka - founder of the amaZulu nation - died on 24 September 1828.

For more on this we cross live to our reporter No-nhla-ka-nipho Magwaza.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Heritage Day | President Ramaphosa's Ten Million Trees Programme also observed
recentItems.description:
President Cyril Ramaphosa will lead South Africa's national Heritage Day celebrations in Oudtshoorn in the Little Karoo today.

The main event at Bongolethu Stadium is being held under the theme, "Celebrating Our Living Heritage: Strengthening the Ties That Bind Us," with a focus on the country's diverse cultural heritage, social cohesion and Ubuntu.

For the latest, we cross live to SABC News reporter Sisipho Ngcumbe in Oudtshoorn, in the Western Cape.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Heritage Day | Moletji residents outside Polokwane celebrate their heritage
recentItems.description:
The people in Moletji outside Polokwane are celebrating their heritage. The event will feature colourful traditional dances by men and women. 

The event is used for the remembrance of their history and culture. 

The annual cultural festival also involves young maidens drawing water from a stream with containers, as part of a ritual of calling for the early Spring rains - resembling the Reed Dance celebrations of the AmaZulu. 

For more on this, we cross live to our reporter Katlego Nyoni.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: KZN School Violence | Communities Demand Action
recentItems.description:
A growing crisis of violence is gripping KwaZulu-Natal, where classrooms and school grounds are increasingly turning into crime scenes. 

From the fatal shooting of a Grade 10 learner at Kwandengezi Intermediate School by an assailant disguised in a uniform, to a deadly robbery at Inanda Comprehensive High, and a violent attack in Bester that left two teenagers dead, the safety of our education system is under severe threat. 

As teacher unions like SADTU sound the alarm over the overwhelming trauma and fear gripping both educators and pupils, we ask: how did our schools become target zones, and what urgent steps must be taken to restore them as safe havens for learning? 

Joining us today to unpack the interventions needed to tackle this crisis is Honourable Zinhle Cele, Kwa Mashu community member and member of the KZN Provincial Legislature. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.
